describes: Way P for a whole house (paint.py): what the corner's p3 (blender/parts/finish/finish.json `painted`, its rules and values used as they are) needs to grow to every wall and opening. `wear` grades the corner's failed paint below the floor by the facts; the rest places what the corner had no fact for. Sizes in metres, values in L*.

clayPaint.describes: The paint the clay's cladding value (finish.json painted.materials.cladding.L) was set for. A house in another paint takes that value scaled by the two paints' L*, so the clay twin and the colour still carry the paint's own value (ox-red is dark), and a house in this paint is unchanged.

light.describes: The street's own lights over the corner's (finish.json painted.light), each as LT1Street's Lighting. Overcast is a CIE overcast sky (docs/research/lighting-and-colour.md: three times brighter at the zenith than at the horizon, a wall seeing at most about 40% of a roof): the hemisphere carries it, sky 1 : equator 0.5 (with the ground's bounce) : ground 0.2, and a quarter more from the brighter cloud round the hidden sun, which casts no hard shadow; what an eave or a verge takes from the wall is the sky it hides (marks.py geo, R). Its sky is drawn (`drawn`, LT1Street.Sky): the CIE overcast, (1 + 2 sin e) / 3 of its zenith, at the radiance of the light it casts (its light on level ground the hemisphere's, equator + 2/3 of sky over equator), and the panes mirror that sky. Its exposure is keyed to the photographs' ladder under cloud (refs 10 and 09, r07's critic): a white front at about L83, 6 to 12 under the sky over the roofs, below the tonemapper's steepest shoulder so its grime and the turn of its faces still read. Before r08 the sky was drawn flat at a third of the light it cast and the street keyed low (0.72), so the white sat level with the sky at L64 to 74. `reflect` is what a pane mirrors across Harbour Row (OS_Glass _Opposite): Barrel Quay's warehouses across the Basin and the Holm's houses and roofs rising behind them (docs/town-plan.md), up to sin 0.15 in uneven blocks, at 0.25 of the horizon's light (tarred, slate and painted fronts under a grey sky), the water and the quay road below at 0.3 of it, and the pane's two faces (refs 04, 10: dark panes at the street, bright sky only in the upper ones seen from below).

wear.describes: p3 is house 107's street front in 1989, its wear `floor` (11.4 years since the coat and 3 let go, over a 13.6-year cycle, at exposure 0.88); a wall's share of p3 is its wear against the floor's, at most 1, so a younger coat fails less than p3 and an older one no more. Wear is (years since the last coat + years neglected) / the upkeep cycle (packs/stavanger-1989/house/paints.json upkeep: the last coat is the cycle's last turn before the house was let go, counted from its building, or a lean-to's) times the wall's exposure (paints.json weather: 1 facing the wet winds, `least` on the lee). Below 1 the corner's strengths, peel heights and run lengths take the share, and each kind of mark runs only from its threshold in `from` (the narrow runs first, then the tongue, then the peel at the casing's foot and on the tops). A sill falling less than `level` a metre is level, and leaks at its end toward the weather. `chalk`: the paint's own age over every painted wall, a wash of `wash` L* (greyer and darker) eased in from a wear of `from` to `full`. `uneven`: each sill fails in its own time, so each opening's tongue is drawn afresh, seeded by the opening: its peel and flake at a `severity` of the wall's, and on each board below the first its peel's width and height times a share from `width` and `height` (at most `top` of the face), or none on a `skip` share of them; the first lap under the sill takes the most water, so board j peels `fall` to the power j of the first, and none below the opening's `boards`.

boarding.describes: The boarded windows (ref 09, Pedersgata 81, 1989): weathered ply, mid-grey and clearly below the white wall the casings frame it in, with big water stains hanging from the head, `stretch` times taller than wide, their tide edges sharp; battens raw sawn wood gone pale grey in the weather, near the wall's own value, so they cross the sheet as light bars. In finish.json painted.boarding's fields, with `colour` [C, h] for way Pc. Replaces the corner's kept variant (c) on every house.

edge.describes: The corner's `edge` with these over it. The neglect, the foot's dirt and the junctions' darks are a film of water and grime over paint and fibre alike, so the bare wood a chip shows takes the share of the page's value shift a multiply gives it, (bareL + 16) / (L + 16) of the cladding (85.3, 52), not the corner's 0.3: where the film greys the paint the chip greys with it and keeps its hard edge (s08's chalk and tongues had brought the two level). The long washes keep the corner's `bareWash`: in a run the fibre stays lighter.

neglect.describes: What a let-go house reads as from the street stop on, in broad shapes only, never fine marks (paint.py neglect_values): a soft grey tongue under each sill, `reach` long and widening by `spread` a metre down; the upper wall grey under the eave's drip, `reach` down; the foot grey from the splash, `reach` up from the drip board; each L* darker at its source, falling off by `power`, its far edge wobbling by `wobble` of its reach over `cell` metres. All at the wall's severity: its wear (paint.py wear) plus `amount` times a neglect event's amount / 1000, eased from `from` (none) to `full`.

roof.describes: A slope's age in broad shapes (paint.py roof_values), in place of the corner's tile-by-tile values on the slopes (the ridge keeps them): the eave course darkest, its reach `courses` courses up the slope; moss and lichen down the pans from the ridge, a lane `width` of a tile's cover wide down each pan, each pan's reach from the ridge a share of the slope in `reach`; the slope that faces away from the sun `shadeL` darker. At the roof's age: years since it was built or last retiled, full at `fullYears`. Replaced tiles only where a fact holds a repair. In the colour too (roof_marks): the lower `share` of the slope greyer and darker, a wash of `wash` L* with a freehand edge; a streak under the chimney as wide as it, widening `spread` a metre down; lichen (the tiles' stain: paler, grey-green) in small rosettes over `octaves` [cell m, weight] on the top courses and the ridge, thinning `down` toward the eave.

splash.describes: The foot's wetting where no drip names it: a gable takes its verge's run-off (finish.json marks.splash.gable); the lean-to's low eave has no gutter and drips its whole length (`leanEave`).

materials.describes: Materials the corner has none of, in finish.json painted.materials' fields: the roof's course planes are its tiles (`roof` takes their values), but lit by their own baked rolls, unflattened (flatUp 0: the s04 A/B, the rolls read as columns down the slope at the street stop and the dashes go); the lean-to's cast plinth, its felt and the chimney's render are guessed values in grey, not yet judged. Lichen on the tiles (their stain) is paler than the tile, `stainDL` below 0.

colour.describes: Way Pc's hue and chroma [C, h] for the materials above, as finish.json painted.colour.mats; the walls' and trims' paint is the pack's (paints.json: a 'repainted' event's, else the era's default), its L* the clay's.
